question.text: In a car race, sound signals emitted by the two cars are detected by a detector on the straight track at the end of the race. The frequency observed for the two cars is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>330</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>360</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> respectively, while the original frequency is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>300</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> for both the cars. The race ends with a separation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> between the cars. Assume both cars move with constant velocity and velocity of sound is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>330</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Find the time taken by the winning car (in second).

solution.text:
330=330330−v1×300⇒  v1=30m s-1

360=330330−v2×300

330−v2=33012×10=275

v2=55m s-1 ; ΔV=25m s-1

100=ΔV×T  ⇒  T=4s
